body: But `"2017-01-01 00:00"` is not a valid datetime format. I'm more inclined to say that the validation was too relaxed and that the marshalled should not have put a value in the entity if it could not be marshalled correctly

I am not sure what kind of format is valid. `2017/01/01 00:00:00` would also cause the same issue.

Also, value of `<input type="datetime-local">` would be `2017-01-01T00:00:00`. It would also cause the same issue (Currently, `Validation::datetime()` doesn't allow this format though).

No, I am. This code is not executed if `_useLocaleParser` is true.
https://github.com/cakephp/cakephp/blob/3b341696e13ad6aed51e330d8e54479a41780512/src/Database/Type/DateTimeType.php#L160-L166
With locale parsing turned off `Y-m-d H:i:s` would be the only acceptable format. So the marshaller returning back string for all other formats is expected isn't it?
Shouldn't the marshaller be able to marshal values that pass validation? Using text input and no validation means you always run the chance of getting text out of the marshaller.

I think we should remove [line 164~166](https://github.com/cakephp/cakephp/blob/3b341696e13ad6aed51e330d8e54479a41780512/src/Database/Type/DateTimeType.php#L164-L166). I think we can assume that the value is already validated, because `Time` or `FrozenTime` object has been created from the string. Although it would allow to convert `+1 day` to `2017-01-15` for example, it is a kind of thing. If users don't want it, they can validate it with the `datetime` validation rule.

Regarding [line 171](https://github.com/cakephp/cakephp/blob/3b341696e13ad6aed51e330d8e54479a41780512/src/Database/Type/DateTimeType.php#L171), I think we should return `null` instead of `$value`. Currently, it may return `0xFF` or `0.1` or something.
I think those lines are to help prevent ambiguous input that result in valid but unintended date values from being marshalled.

> ambiguous input

Do you mean `01/01/01 00:00:00` for example? But currently, the returned value will be embedded into SQL statement without using timezone settings defined in `app.php`. I don't think it is a correct behavior:
```sql
SET published = '01/01/01 00:00:00'
```
If we could return `Time` or `FrozenTime` object, it could use the timezone settings:
```sql
SET published = '2001-01-01 09:00:00'
```

I forgot about  #6571 . My example above is not true.

So is it a feature? Then I will open a pull request to change the return type to `\Cake\Chronos\ChronosInterface|\DateTimeInterface|string|null`.
